name: Khmer nationalism
summary: Khmer nationalism holds that the Khmers are a distinct people and nation, heirs of Angkor, whose language, culture, Buddhism and territory must be defended and revived. Its constant theme is the Vietnamese (and to a lesser degree Thai) as the hereditary threat, with grievance over Kampuchea Krom and distrust of the Vietnamese minority. Its strands differ on the monarchy: royalist (Sihanouk, the 1993 Kingdom), republican (Son Ngoc Thanh, Lon Nol) and communist (the Khmer Rouge).
scope: The doctrine on the national question (identity, territory, sovereignty, language, culture, minorities, kin abroad, means) from the 1930s Nagaravatta circle of Son Ngoc Thanh through the Sangkum, Lon Nol's neo-Khmerism and the Khmer Republic, Democratic Kampuchea's nationalist texts (Black Paper) and today's nationalism of the CPP and the opposition. Based on the Black Paper, Pol Pot's 1977 speech for its national lines only, the 1993 constitution's nation-defining articles, Mak and Heder. The economic, social and regime-form programmes of the Sangkum, the Khmer Republic, DK and the CPP are not part of it and are null unless the nationalist texts state them as part of the national cause. Lon Nol's New Khmerism and Sihanouk's speeches could not be read in full.
